catalog_locator: sec. 5.2 'Stress', p. 24 (with sec. 5.1, 5.3 on the same page); tone: sec. 7 'Tone', p. 26
catalog_quote: 5.1 Ambiguous Segments ... For representation and tone, long vowels are analyzed as two consecutive vowels for they represent two moras. For syllable patterns however, they count as one unit. 5.2 Stress Gbaya has no phonemic stress. It is therefore not analyzed here. 5.3 Intonation There are different intonation patterns for affirmative clauses, commands and questions. (cf. Samarin 66 p.31). They are not analyzed here. ... 7. TONE Gbaya has two phonemic tones. Utterance level intonation is used phonemically for questions and commands. There are two contrasting pitches, one high, one low (Samarin 66 § 113) (Montgolfier 75/3 p.5) and rise and fall only on long vowels. ... Tones are lexical, except for verbs and their derivations. Tones are grammatical on verbs, e.g. aspect, but predictable and redundant with their suffixes
